name: Paid online research studies (Prolific)
summary: Take part in paid online research studies when you match a study's criteria; this is research participation, not a job.
whatYouDo: You fill in a demographic profile, then claim studies (mostly surveys and online experiments) that appear in your dashboard on a first-come, first-served basis. Each study lists its reward and estimated time. Once the researcher approves your submission, the reward goes to your balance, which you cash out to PayPal.
appeal: Researchers must pay at least £6 / $8 per hour and are advised to pay £9 / $12 (Prolific rules)
Prolific charges no cash-out fee, and the minimum cash-out is a low £6/$6
You pick studies whenever you like, with no set hours
Long-established platform with a public participant help centre
watchOuts: Not a job: studies aren't guaranteed, and 2026 third-party reviews say new sign-ups may be waitlisted
Study supply is the most common complaint: some days nothing matches your profile, and popular studies fill fast
The pay rate uses estimated or median completion time, so your real hourly earnings can be lower

Accounts can be put 'On hold' (for example for VPN or location mismatch, many rejections, multiple accounts, or using AI or automation), and Prolific doesn't give a specific reason. You can appeal through support
Payout is PayPal only (through Hyperwallet), in GBP or USD. PayPal may charge for currency conversion, and your PayPal name must match your Prolific details

compensation.notes: Prolific's researcher rules set a minimum reward rate of £6 / $8 per hour and recommend £9 / $12, based on estimated or median completion time. Third-party 2026 reviews report a wide range of effective rates, from about $8–15/hr down to far lower once unpaid waiting and screening time is counted. Rewards are paid in GBP or USD, not CAD.

reliability.notes: Studies are first-come, first-served and depend on your demographics. 2026 reviews describe days with no eligible studies and frequent 'study full' messages. No official supply statistics were found.

fees: Prolific charges no cash-out fee (official); PayPal may charge for currency conversion.
applicationSteps: Confirm your country of residence is on Prolific's supported list (Canada is listed)
Create a participant account (you may be put on a waitlist)
Pass account and identity verification and complete your profile questions
Link a PayPal account whose details match your Prolific details
Claim studies you qualify for, and cash out from £6/$6 (your first four cash-outs wait 72 hours)
fitsIf: You want occasional, flexible small earnings from your computer and can live with unpredictable study supply.
notFitIf: You need dependable weekly income or don't want identity checks and PayPal-only payouts.

name: Paid user research sessions (User Interviews)
summary: Apply to occasional paid product-research sessions (interviews, surveys, tests) run by companies; this is research participation, not a job.
whatYouDo: You build a participant profile and answer screener surveys for studies that interest you. If a researcher picks you, you join a session such as a video interview or survey and receive an incentive afterwards.
appeal: Canada is a supported participant country for projects that User Interviews runs itself ('Recruit' projects)
A single session can pay well for its length (one third-party review reports about US$45 per study on average)
You can redeem incentives in your local currency
watchOuts: Very occasional: User Interviews itself estimates 1–2 study invitations every 6 months
Screeners can be long, and you may hear nothing for days or weeks (third-party review)
When User Interviews pays you, it's a Tremendous digital gift card or prepaid Visa, not PayPal, Venmo or a bank transfer
Incentives are shown in USD, and one redeemed in the wrong currency can't be reissued
Payment can take up to 10 business days after the session

compensation.notes: No official average. A third-party review (The Work at Home Woman) reports about US$45 per completed study in its 2026 data, up from $29 in 2021. Each incentive is set by the researcher and varies with study length and type.

reliability.notes: Officially, a participant can expect 1–2 invitations every 6 months, and the first selection can take time.

applicationSteps: Create a participant profile and keep it complete and accurate
Apply to studies by answering their screener surveys
If selected, attend the scheduled session
Redeem the incentive through Tremendous, choosing the correct currency for Canada
fitsIf: You don't mind filling in screeners now and then for the chance of a well-paid one-off session.
notFitIf: You need regular income, or you want cash to PayPal or your bank rather than gift cards.

name: Paid research interviews and focus groups (Respondent)
summary: Apply to paid interviews, focus groups and surveys that companies run with consumers and professionals; this is research participation, not a job.
whatYouDo: You create a verified profile and apply to studies by answering a screener, then the researcher decides whom to invite. Respondent focuses on remote qualitative interviews, and the incentive is paid after the session.
appeal: Canada is one of Respondent's 21 primary recruiting markets
Studies are often higher-value interviews and focus groups (third-party reviews cite roughly $50–$250 per study)
Payout through Tremendous offers many redemption options
watchOuts: Not a job: you can be screened out by the screener or by the researcher, often without being told (G2 user reviews)
A fulfillment fee of 5% or $1, whichever is higher, comes off each incentive
Profiles are verified by phone, email and LinkedIn, and professional studies may expect a work profile
One review-site complaint (2025) says a study was still unpaid four weeks later
Older reviews say payouts go to PayPal, but Respondent's current help says Tremendous gift cards, so check payout options before counting on cash

compensation.notes: No official pay figures were retrieved. Third-party review titles advertise about $50–$250 per focus group and '$100+/hour', which are marketing-style claims. Each researcher sets the incentive, and the fulfillment fee is deducted from it.

reliability.notes: The researcher decides who is selected. G2 reviewers say they often aren't picked, and popular studies draw many applicants.

fees: A 5% or $1 fulfillment fee, whichever is higher, is deducted from each incentive (official help).
applicationSteps: Create a participant profile and verify your phone and email (LinkedIn may be requested)
Browse studies and answer the screener for ones that fit
If the researcher picks you, schedule and attend the session
Receive the incentive, minus the fulfillment fee, through Tremendous
fitsIf: You have a specific consumer or professional background that researchers seek and are comfortable on video calls.
notFitIf: You want steady income or dislike verification steps such as connecting LinkedIn.

name: Website and app tester (UserTesting contributor)
summary: Get paid small amounts to try websites and apps while speaking your thoughts aloud on a screen recording; occasional paid tests, not a job.
whatYouDo: You answer screener questions for tests in your dashboard. If you qualify, you complete tasks on a website or app while recording your screen and voice and saying what you think. Every test in your feed shows its pay before you start.
appeal: Canada is one of UserTesting's seven standard contributor countries
Pay for each test is shown up front in your feed
Tests are short: third-party reviews commonly cite about $10 for a roughly 20-minute unmoderated test
The practice test can be done in English or French (or German)
watchOuts: Not a job: screeners often disqualify you, and tests come and go (third-party reviews)
Signing up includes a practice test that reviews describe as unpaid
Payment is PayPal only, about 14 days after each test
If you submit an incomplete test instead of reporting a problem, the payment is cancelled
You have to talk aloud while your screen is recorded

compensation.notes: UserTesting's help centre says pay depends on customer demand, test type and tasks, and is shown for each test. Third-party reviews commonly put a typical unmoderated test at about $10, with longer or live sessions paying more (one site advertises $10–$120). The $10 is a typical figure, not a guaranteed minimum.

reliability.notes: There's no official data on test volume. Third-party reviews report high screener disqualification rates.

applicationSteps: Start sign-up on UserTesting's contributor page (it tells you whether your location qualifies)
Verify your email and connect a PayPal account in good standing
Complete your profile
Record the practice test in English, French or German
Take screeners in your dashboard and complete the tests you qualify for
fitsIf: You're comfortable thinking aloud on a recording and want short, occasional paid tasks.
notFitIf: You need regular income or don't want to be recorded while you talk.

You do it on your phone, on your own schedule within mission deadlines

name: Paid university research studies (University of Toronto participant pools)
organization: University of Toronto (psychology departments and labs)
summary: Sign up to University of Toronto participant registries to be contacted for paid psychology studies; occasional research participation, not a job.
whatYouDo: You register with a campus participant pool or sign-up system and are invited to, or sign up for, studies you're eligible for. Sessions in the St. George adult pool usually last 1–2 hours, and some labs run computer tasks or MRI scans.
appeal: Official pay at one pool: $18/hour for the St. George Adult Volunteer Pool
Community members, not just students, can register at the St. George, Mississauga (UTM) and Scarborough (UTSC) campuses
Some pools specifically want older adults (40–80 or 55–80), a group online panels often underserve
watchOuts: Only practical if you can get to a Toronto-area campus for in-person studies
Eligibility depends on the study, with age bands such as 55–80, 40–80 or healthy adults 18–35
Invitations are occasional, and registering doesn't guarantee any studies
Some UofT recruitment pages are years old, so confirm a pool is active before relying on it
Rotman's paid pool (about $10/hour) is aimed at students, not the general public

compensation.notes: The St. George Adult Volunteer Pool states $18/hour (ages 55–80, sessions usually 1–2 h). The other UofT community pools reviewed don't give a rate in the text retrieved. The student-oriented Rotman pool is about $10/hour.

reliability.notes: Recruitment depends on active studies and their age bands. No volume data was found.

applicationSteps: Choose the pool for your campus: the Adult Volunteer Pool (St. George), the UTM Psychological & Brain Sciences sign-up system, or the UTSC Community Adult Volunteer Panel
Register with your name, contact details and age
Wait to be contacted, or sign up for paid studies you're eligible for
Attend the session and receive your compensation
fitsIf: You live near a University of Toronto campus (especially if you're an older adult) and want occasional paid study sessions.
notFitIf: You can't travel to campus or you need predictable income.

name: Freelance client work through Upwork
summary: Sell services to clients by sending proposals for projects posted on Upwork's freelance marketplace.
whatYouDo: You build a profile, then spend 'Connects' to send proposals to clients' job posts. If hired, you agree hourly or fixed-price terms and deliver the work. Upwork deducts its service fee before you withdraw your earnings to your bank.
appeal: Large marketplace where clients post jobs you can bid on
The fee is shown before you send a proposal and stays fixed for that contract
Withdrawals straight to a local bank cost a flat $0.99 USD
Reviews and a track record can lead to repeat clients
watchOuts: Since May 2025 the freelancer service fee varies from 0% to 15% per contract (third-party guides say about 10% is typical)
Proposals cost Connects ($0.15 each), and many jobs need about 6–16 or more; third-party guides say Connects spent on proposals generally aren't refunded
New profiles can be rejected when a skill area is crowded (Upwork Community reports)
Forum posts say new freelancers often spend their Connects and get no interviews
Optional Freelancer Plus costs $19.99/month
Canadian bank fees and currency-conversion costs may apply on top

compensation.notes: You set your rate or bid. No earnings data was checked in this pass. Take-home pay is after the 0–15% service fee, Connects spending and withdrawal costs.

reliability.notes: Work depends on winning proposals. Forum anecdotes describe new freelancers getting no interviews, and there's no official win-rate data.

fees: Freelancer service fee varies 0–15% per contract and is shown before you propose. Basic accounts pay 5% on direct contracts. Connects cost $0.15 each (minimum 10). Freelancer Plus is optional at $19.99/month. Direct to Local Bank withdrawal costs $0.99 USD, with a $5 USD minimum.
applicationSteps: Create a freelancer profile focused on a specific skill clients want
Wait for profile approval (crowded skill areas may be declined)
Send targeted proposals using free or purchased Connects
Check the service fee shown on each proposal or offer
Set up a withdrawal method such as Direct to Local Bank and withdraw your earnings
fitsIf: You have a skill clients pay for, can write persuasive proposals, and can afford some upfront Connects cost while you build reviews.
notFitIf: You need income within days or can't afford to spend money on bids that may not pay off.

appeal: Lots of posted projects to bid on
